correctness.rationale: The object and language are precisely defined. Four rank-at-most-three sentences detect index cutoffs 2,3,4,5. Their endpoint tests follow from the Brandt multiplication law. The Duplicator first preserves equality of at most four coordinate indices in two moves, then matches the third exactly unless two fresh indices would raise the union to six; in that unique case all previous endpoints are distinct and replacement by (source of first, target of second) preserves every equality/relational-multiplication atom. This establishes equivalence for all n,m>=5. Exact full-table three-round type computations for n=1..6 and orbit-profile saturation for n=5,6,7 reproduce the five classes. The finite checks alone are not treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Compared the exact implication (five rank-three theories of B_n with a sharp n=5 cutoff and 26-element in-family kernel), not keyword or title similarity. The fully inspected Gelbaum--Schanuel 1980 Theorem 1 characterizes semigroups of matrix units via a unique middle factor and contains no 3-round finite-index comparison. Mitchell 2004 treats independent-set maxima, Gray--Ruskuc 2007 generating ranks, and Gilbert--Samman 2010 endomorphism seminear-rings. Relevant indexed research records yielded non-equivalent results but no direct covering statement. Full-text access was limited for several cited papers, so residual implicit or unindexed coverage is possible.
residual_risks: Full texts of Mitchell 2004, Gray--Ruskuc 2007 and Gilbert--Samman 2010 were not materially read; comparisons are limited to accessible abstracts.
Historical publications could contain implicit or equivalent first-order EF classifications that were not indexed under the searched aliases.
The research database search is approximate and cannot prove novelty, especially where a paper uses categorical-semigroup or Rees-matrix terminology.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification of low-depth elementary equivalence for a classical family of inverse semigroups, with a sharp five-index stabilization threshold and optimal 26-element in-family representative. The folding lemma explains an otherwise nonobvious expressive limitation of three selected semigroup elements, and the four explicit separating sentences turn a crude eventual bound into a sharp structural theorem. The result is not simply a known table or arbitrary numerical slice.
